description: QodoWars is a solo-led initiative driven by a passion for space exploration, technology, and creative storytelling. I aim to bring NASA's forgotten lunar and Martian equipment to life through an engaging digital experience. I'm looking for passionate collaborators with skills in space research, web development, AI/ML, graphic design, and storytelling to join me in building something innovative!
summary:
ASTRAFORGE is an interactive space mission simulation platform that transforms students into mission commanders responsible for building and managing a sustainable lunar or Martian outpost.

Through an engaging, decision-driven experience, students manage six essential survival systems: oxygen, water, food, energy, radiation protection, and temperature. Every engineering decision creates trade-offs. Expanding a greenhouse improves food production but increases energy consumption, while stronger radiation shielding improves crew safety but requires additional construction resources.

The simulator introduces dynamic mission events, resource management, emergency scenarios, and an AI-powered learning mentor that explains the science behind each decision in simple, student-friendly language.

ASTRAFORGE addresses the challenge of making complex space engineering concepts accessible, interactive, and enjoyable. Instead of simply learning scientific facts, students experiment, encounter failures, compare strategies, and discover how engineering decisions determine mission success.

Our goal is to inspire the next generation of space explorers while developing their scientific curiosity, critical thinking, and problem-solving skills.
details:
ASTRAFORGE – Junior Astronaut Mission Trainer

Overview

ASTRAFORGE is an interactive educational space mission simulator designed to help students understand the engineering challenges involved in establishing sustainable human settlements on the Moon and Mars.

Rather than presenting space science through static lessons, ASTRAFORGE puts students in the role of mission commanders, allowing them to make decisions, manage resources, respond to emergencies, and experience the consequences of their engineering choices.

How It Works

Students begin by selecting a lunar or Martian mission and configuring their outpost. They manage six interconnected survival systems:

  • Oxygen: Maintaining breathable air and life-support operations.
  • Water: Managing consumption, storage, and recycling.
  • Food: Balancing greenhouse production and crew requirements.
  • Energy: Managing solar generation, batteries, and power consumption.
  • Radiation: Protecting astronauts through appropriate shielding.
  • Temperature: Maintaining safe habitat conditions.

The simulation advances through mission days. Students can construct upgrades, allocate resources, and respond to dynamic events such as solar storms, dust storms, equipment failures, and food production problems.

Every decision affects other systems. For example, expanding food production increases energy demand, while installing additional radiation shielding requires construction resources.

An AI-powered Mission Mentor provides simple explanations of scientific concepts and helps students understand the consequences of their decisions.

NASA Data and Scientific Foundation

The project uses NASA educational and scientific resources to ground its planetary environments, mission scenarios, and learning content in real space science. NASA resources are used to distinguish the environmental challenges of lunar and Martian exploration.

Intended Impact

ASTRAFORGE makes complex space engineering concepts accessible to younger learners through experiential learning. It encourages critical thinking, resource conservation, scientific curiosity, decision-making, and problem-solving.

The platform aims to make students understand that successful space exploration is not just about reaching another world; it is about designing systems that can sustain human life.

Technology Stack

Frontend: React, Vite, Tailwind CSS
Backend: Python and FastAPI
Simulation: Python-based resource management and mission logic
Visualizations: Recharts
AI Integration: Google Gemini API
Deployment: Render

Creativity and Innovation

ASTRAFORGE combines educational gaming, resource-management simulation, engineering trade-offs, dynamic mission events, and AI-assisted explanations in one interactive learning environment.

Its central innovation is learning through consequences: students do not simply memorize the requirements of a space mission; they experiment with those requirements and discover why balancing interconnected systems is essential for survival.

Design Considerations

The experience is designed to be intuitive and age-appropriate, with visual resource indicators, understandable explanations, interactive controls, meaningful feedback, and opportunities to retry failed missions.

The simulation is educational and illustrative, with clearly identified assumptions rather than claiming to be a certified engineering model.
